readerQuestion: Can a personal AI control surface make trust and authority understandable without asking people to manage it like a system administrator?
centralTension: The control surface must make AI authority legible without exposing the machinery as a technical permission system.
verifiedObservations: The issue proposes a personal AI control surface called My AI Rules.
The screen is organized around what the AI knows, what it can use, what it can do, and when it must ask before acting.
Each group uses ordinary-language states rather than system-administration terminology.
The issue describes a proposed screen structure and does not claim that it has been built or tested.
inferences: Visible, ordinary-language rules may make the boundary of delegated authority easier to inspect.
recommendedStructure: How the control surface is grouped
unresolvedQuestions: Would people understand the difference between Ask first and Ask me across knowledge, access, and action?
How should the interface show that the AI complied with a rule after an action occurs?
Which sensitive actions need categories beyond the proposed money, family, health, work, contact, change, and deletion boundaries?
nextAction: Generate a bounded prototype-note and review the grouped controls, proposed-state warning, and page treatment locally.

reasons: The issue supplies the screen purpose, group structure, permission states, design principle, and explicit proposed nature of the artifact.

prototypeNote.designProblem: Child-level means that trust controls should be instantly understandable, not that the user is a child. The design idea is that the user should not manage the AI like a system administrator.
prototypeNote.interactionChoice: The proposed artifact is a child-level personal AI control surface called My AI Rules. The screen answers four questions: what does the AI know, what can it use, what can it do, and when must it ask first? The control surface communicates what is allowed, what requires permission, and what is off-limits.

interactionGroups.title: What my AI knows
items: What my AI knows includes name, family, projects, schedule, likes, and writing style, with Keep, Ask first, and Forget states.

interactionGroups.title: What my AI can use
items: What my AI can use includes calendar, email, notes, photos, location, and contacts, with Yes, Ask me, and No states.

interactionGroups.title: What my AI can do
items: What my AI can do includes helping the user think, drafting messages, creating reminders, organizing things, suggesting plans, and talking to other apps, with Always okay, Ask first, and Never states.

interactionGroups.title: Before you act, ask me if
items: Before acting, it must ask about money, family, health, work, contacting another person, and changing or deleting something.

designPrinciples: The user should be able to establish ordinary-language house rules and see that the AI is following them.
prototypeNote.currentState: This is a proposed screen structure. The issue does not claim that it has been built or tested.
